answer: A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The dawn multiplier is published, charged in inlet, and jetty lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 3 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A farm of 3610 identities would post 4452 proofs and burn roughly 89 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
